get.description: One row per admin write (#313 Tasks 1-2), newest first by ActionUtc then Id (a tiebreaker: many rows from the same write batch can share one ActionUtc instant). EntityType and EntityId together answer 'history of this row'; ActorId and Action narrow by who/what — ActorId matches case-insensitively, EntityType does not. FromUtc/ToUtc bound the range and are both inclusive; pass an explicit time-of-day, since a date alone (e.g. toUtc=2026-09-02) means midnight at the start of that day and so excludes everything that happened on it. All filters are optional and combine with AND. EntityId is null on a create of an entity with a store-generated key (the database assigns it during the very write this row records, so it does not exist yet) — such a row can never be found through the EntityId filter and is identified through its After payload instead, which holds the created entity's full property set.

Proxies GitHub's run list for the CI workflow (GitHub:Workflow, default ci.yml), newest first. Optional 'branch' filters to one branch; 'limit' is 1–50, default 20. Cached for 60 seconds. Test counts are not part of a run: read them from GET /admin/ci/runs/{id}/tests. 503 when GitHub:Token is not set.

Reads the test-results.json from the run's test-results artifact: totals, then each test project with every test's outcome, duration and failure message. 404 when the run doesn't exist, has no report (still running, or stopped before its tests reported), or its report has expired. Cached by artifact, since an artifact never changes. 503 when GitHub:Token is not set.

get.summary: List every table the admin data browser can read
get.description: Slug, display name and current row count for each table registered in BrowsableTables.

get.summary: Read one browsable table's rows, masked and paginated
get.description: Strictly read-only. Every column SensitiveProperties marks sensitive is replaced with "<redacted>" server-side before this response is built — the full value never leaves the API from this endpoint (a full reveal, audited, is a separate future endpoint). 'sort' is a column name, optionally prefixed with '-' for descending (e.g. sort=-CreatedUtc); paging is stable even without an explicit sort, via an always-appended primary-key tiebreaker. 'filter' is 'column:value' — exact match for a non-string column, case-insensitive contains for a string column, split on the first ':' only so a value such as an ISO-8601 timestamp can itself contain colons. On a string column, a value of exactly '*' means 'has a value' — not null, and not blank (non-empty after trimming whitespace); '*' anywhere else in the value is still a literal character to find by contains. On a non-string column '*' is not special-cased and is simply an unparseable value, a 400. Both 'sort' and 'filter' column names are matched case-sensitively (e.g. 'CreatedUtc', not 'createdUtc') against the table's exposed-column whitelist and rejected with 400 if unknown, wrong-case or sensitive — a sensitive column would otherwise let a filter be used to guess a masked value one character at a time.

post.summary: Reveal one sensitive value, audited
post.description: The escape hatch around the data browser's server-side masking (#315). Only a column registered in SensitiveProperties for the table's entity may be revealed — any other column, including an already-unmasked one, is a 400. Every successful reveal writes an admin_audit_log row (Action=Reveal) recording who revealed which column on which row and when; Before/After are never populated and the value itself never appears in the row, only its column name. The audit row is committed before this response is returned — a failed audit write fails the whole request with a 500 rather than returning a value with no audit trail. Responses carry Cache-Control: no-store. Rate-limited per actor (RateLimiting:AdminReveal), far tighter than the rest of the admin API: this endpoint exists to be used rarely, not as a second browsing mode.

get.description: The same search, inputs and responses as GET /flights/search, for the admin panel. Each row can be posted unmodified to POST /admin/travelers/{id}/flights. Returns the flight with its current status and its 50 most recent status events, most recently recorded first (by event id) — the record of what the sync actually saw, in the order it saw it. Not ordered by effectiveAtUtc, which can move backwards when an estimate returns to an earlier value. Not the full history: a long-tracked flight polled every couple of minutes accumulates status-event rows without bound. StatusHistoryTruncated is true when the cap actually cut rows off; when it is, see GET /admin/data/flight-status-events for the rest.

post.summary: Sync flight status
post.description: Syncs the flight's status now. A flight not yet inside the provider's live-status window makes no provider call, and a flight no traveler tracks makes no call and has its sync plan cleared; both return { updated: false }. Otherwise { updated: true } means an event was recorded — a new status, a revised time for the status the flight already has, or a gate, terminal or baggage-claim change on the current status — and { updated: false } means none was, which still allows a revised estimated arrival or aircraft type to have been saved. Once this month's flight data budget is used up, only a flight in its near-departure window (by default, from 4 hours before departure until 30 minutes after it lands) makes a call; any other returns 503. Returns 404 if no flight with that id exists — unlike the traveler route, which answers 403 because it checks the tracking link first. 503 also covers the flight data provider throttling requests, not only the monthly budget; 502 is returned when the provider is unreachable or answers unexpectedly, and 500 for a provider configuration problem. Like every /admin route, an unauthenticated caller gets 401 and a caller without the admin role gets 403; neither is declared per-route because both are identical across the whole admin surface.

get.description: Runs every registered health check with no predicate — including 'aeroapi' and 'apns', tagged 'external' and excluded from the load-balancer probe at /health/ready — and always responds 200, even when the overall status is Unhealthy. Also reports process/build info (version, build SHA, uptime), pending EF Core migrations, the flight-status sync's last-run heartbeat, and the reference verification job's last-cycle heartbeat with its pending request count. Exception detail on individual checks and both jobs' last errors render outside Production only.

get.summary: Dashboard card counts: totals, new in a period, verified
get.description: For travelers, flights, airlines, airports, lounges and loyalty programs: the total, how many were added in the period with a per-bucket series, and verified/unverified counts (null for travelers and flights). 'period' is 24h, 7d, 30d or 90d (default 7d), resolved to whole hourly (24h) or UTC-day buckets ending with the current one, so NewInPeriod always equals the sum of Series. 'Added' is CreatedUtc, or FirstSeenAt for airlines and airports; rows with no known date and seeded airlines and airports never count as new.

Email and every device token are masked as "<redacted>"; reveal the real value via POST /admin/data/{table}/{id}/reveal. TrackedFlights is capped at 50, newest first; TrackedFlightsTruncated is true when the cap actually cut rows off, and the full relationship is available via GET /admin/data/traveler-flights. Device tokens and loyalty memberships are not capped.

post.summary: Track a flight for a traveler
post.description: Adds a flight to this traveler's tracking list, exactly as POST /flights does for the signed-in traveler. A row from GET /admin/flights/search can be posted here unmodified. Tracking a flight the traveler already tracks changes nothing and still returns 201 with its flightId. An unknown traveler is a 404 and writes nothing. The same cap as POST /flights applies: at the traveler's limit of flights tracked at a time, tracking another returns 409 and writes nothing.

delete.description: Removes a stale APNs device token. This is NOT a device revocation: it only stops push notifications from reaching that token, and the client re-registers a fresh one on its next launch.

get.description: Proxies FlightAware's own GET /account/usage report — calls, pages and cost for the range, broken down by operation, alongside the configured monthly budget and the next available outbound throttle slot. Optional 'start' and 'end' are UTC instants; they default to the current UTC month to date. AeroAPI serves at most one year of history, so an earlier start is rejected. Cached for 10 minutes, matching FlightAware's own refresh cadence.

get.summary: List the verification sources that can check an entity type
get.description: The registered sources whose supported entity types include 'entityType', ordered by name, with each one's cost per row lookup. 'entityType' is required and must be exactly Airport, Airline or Country; anything else is a 400. An empty list is a valid answer: no source checks Airline yet.

get.summary: Counts of reference-data rows that need attention
get.description: One entry per VerificationEntityType (Airport, Airline, Country), always all three, in enum order, with a count of 0 rather than an omitted entry. A row needs attention when its most recent automated check found a problem: IsVerified is false and VerificationIssue is set -- the state only the verification job's mismatch and not-found paths leave behind. A row that has simply never been checked (IsVerified false, no issue) does not count. No parameters.

get.summary: An entity's most recent verification checks
get.description: The entity's checks, newest first, at most 'limit' (default 5, range 1-50). Not a page: no total, and the full history stays browsable at GET /admin/data/verification-requests. Each row's sources, differences and source values come back typed, not as the stored comma-joined or JSON strings: sources is the list of source names checked; differences is { column, ours, source, sourceName } per differing column; sourceValues is keyed by source name, each value a map of column name to what that source reported. 'entityType' is required and must be exactly Airport, Airline or Country; 'entityKey' is required and canonicalised before matching, so a lower-case country code finds the upper-case row. An entity with no checks yet is an empty list, never a 404.

post.summary: Queue verification checks for reference-data rows
post.description: Queues one Pending request per key, checked against every selected source, with trigger 'admin', the caller as requested_by, and the selected sources' summed per-row cost as the estimated cost. Keys are not checked for existence: a missing entity completes as Error when the job runs it. A repeated key, or an entity that already has an open request, is counted as skipped -- never the #418 error cooldown, which gates only the flight-tracking trigger, not this route. 400 when entityType is not Airport, Airline or Country; keys or sources are empty; there are more than 1000 keys; a key is malformed for the entity type (the error names it, e.g. 'Keys[1]'); or a source is unknown or does not support the entity type. Queue rows are not audited; requested_by records who asked.

post.summary: Accept one source's values for a mismatched check
post.description: Writes the chosen source's values to the entity for only the columns that source reported as different, verifies the entity with that source as the caller, and saves once. The entity write is audited as an Update; the request itself stays Mismatch. 400 when 'source' is blank, is not one of the request's sources, or has no stored values. 404 when the request or the entity no longer exists. 409 when the request is not Mismatch; the entity has an open verification request (accept once it has finished); a differing column has changed since the check; a value cannot be parsed or would empty a required column; the row would break the admin edit's rules; a new unique code already belongs to another row; or a new country code is not one of our countries. The edit-rules check validates the whole row, as the admin edit does, so an existing invalid value in a column the source did not touch also returns 409, naming that column.

post.summary: Check an entity again with an earlier request's sources
post.description: Queues a new Pending request for the same entity type, key and sources, with trigger 'admin', the caller as requested_by, and the sources' current cost. The earlier request is left as it is. 400 when one of its sources is no longer registered or no longer supports the entity type. 404 when the request does not exist. 409 when the entity already has an open request -- never the #418 error cooldown, which gates only the flight-tracking trigger: an admin retry always queues regardless of it.

get.summary: Search flights by route or flight number on a date
get.description:
Searches scheduled flights to populate the 'add flight' picker. Each returned row has exactly the same shape as TrackFlightRequest (flightNumber, serviceDate, departureAirportIata, arrivalAirportIata, scheduledDepartureUtc, scheduledArrivalUtc), so a result can be posted straight to POST /flights, unmodified, to track it.

Search criteria (query params):
- date (required): the departure date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must fall within the provider's rolling past/future horizon.
- from / to (optional): departure and arrival airport as 3-letter IATA codes (e.g. LHR, JFK). Case-insensitive. Must be supplied together.
- flightNumber (optional): an IATA flight code — a 2-character airline prefix containing at least one letter, followed by 1–4 digits and an optional trailing letter (e.g. BA123, 6E4120, BA123A). Case-insensitive. The same rule POST /flights applies, so any flightNumber this endpoint accepts is trackable.
- includeCodeshares (optional, default false): when true, includes codeshare-marketed rows for the same physical departure alongside the operating flight's own row; when false, only the operating flight's own row is returned.

You must provide either a full route (both from and to) OR a flightNumber, in addition to date; otherwise the request is rejected with 400.

Each result is one flight designator — the same aircraft sold under several marketing numbers (e.g. TK1028 is also 6E4120, MS9668, RJ3710 and SQ6228) appears as one row per number, not grouped. There is no separate 'operating carrier' field: the airline is always the first two characters of the result's own flightNumber.

Responses:
- 200: list of matching flights (empty list when the provider responds successfully but nothing matches).
- 400: invalid/insufficient parameters.
- 500: server-side configuration issue with the flight data provider.
- 502: the flight data provider was unreachable or returned an unexpected error.
- 503: the flight data provider is throttling requests, or this month's flight data budget is nearly used up, so only searches already cached are answered; retry after the period in the Retry-After header.
- 429: too many searches from this caller (per signed-in traveler, or per client IP when anonymous); retry after the period in the Retry-After header.

Returns a paginated list of flights the authenticated traveler is tracking. Supports ?page and ?pageSize (default 50, max 200). countsTowardCap is true while the status sync still polls the flight, which is what occupies a slot against the tracking cap POST /flights enforces; it turns false once the flight has landed or been cancelled for long enough, or its arrival time passed a day ago without a landing being reported. activeTrackedFlights counts every flight of this traveler that still occupies a slot, across all pages, and trackingCap is the configured limit — so remaining capacity is trackingCap minus activeTrackedFlights, floored at zero, without paging through the list. A traveler grandfathered above the cap, or one whose cap was later lowered in configuration, reports more active flights than the cap. Both numbers are as of this response: tracking can still be refused if capacity is used in the meantime. total is a different number — it counts every flight the traveler tracks, including ones that no longer occupy a slot. Tracking a flight the traveler already tracks still succeeds at the cap.

post.summary: Track a flight
post.description: Adds a flight to the authenticated traveler's tracking list. A row returned by GET /flights/search can be posted here unmodified — this body is exactly that shape. If the flight already exists in the system (same airline, number, and service date) it is reused; otherwise a new flight record is created. The airline is derived from the first two characters of FlightNumber (e.g. 'BA123' -> 'BA', '6E4120' -> '6E'); there is no separate airline field. Body fields: FlightNumber (e.g. 'BA123' or '6E4120'), ServiceDate (YYYY-MM-DD), DepartureAirportIata, ArrivalAirportIata, ScheduledDepartureUtc, ScheduledArrivalUtc. A traveler can track a limited number of flights at a time. GET /flights reports the limit in force as trackingCap, and how many slots are in use as activeTrackedFlights (#397). A flight counts until its status sync stops: by default 30 minutes after it lands or is cancelled, or a day after its arrival time if no landing is reported. Tracking another returns 409 and adds nothing; tracking a flight the traveler already tracks still returns 201. Rate-limited per traveler: too many tracking requests return 429 with a Retry-After header. Returns 404 if the airline or either airport in the request is not known to the system.

delete.description: Removes the specified flight from the authenticated traveler's tracking list. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric ID returned when the flight was tracked. Idempotent: untracking a flight the traveler does not track also returns 204, so there is no 404.

patch.description: Enables or disables push notifications for a tracked flight. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric flight ID. Body: { "notify": true } (true to enable, false to disable). Notifications are delivered via APNs to device tokens registered for the traveler. Returns 404 if the traveler does not track this flight — unlike DELETE /flights/{flightId}, which is idempotent and returns 204 either way.

get.description: Returns the flight's full status-event history — every event, not a page — most recently recorded first. The order is the order events were recorded (by event id), not effectiveAtUtc, which can move backwards when an estimate returns to an earlier value; so the first row is the flight's current status. Each event captures the status code, gate/terminal info, baggage claim, and the time it became effective. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric flight ID. Returns 403 if the authenticated traveler does not track this flight — including when no flight with that id exists, so the response does not reveal whether a flight id is real to someone who does not track it. There is no 404.

post.summary: Manually sync flight status
post.description: Triggers an on-demand status refresh for the specified flight. Whether the external flight data provider is queried depends on the flight's sync mode: a flight not yet inside the provider's live-status window makes no provider call. A flight synced within the manual-sync cooldown (5 minutes by default) makes no call either. Once this month's flight data budget is used up, only a flight in its near-departure window (by default, from 4 hours before departure until 30 minutes after it lands) is refreshed; any other returns 503. 503 also covers the flight data provider throttling requests, not only the monthly budget; 502 is returned when the provider is unreachable or answers unexpectedly, and 500 for a provider configuration problem. Returns { updated: true } when an event was recorded — a new status, a revised time for the status the flight already has, or a gate, terminal or baggage-claim change on the current status — and { updated: false } when none was: no call was made, or the response repeated what was already recorded. { updated: false } still does not mean nothing changed: a revised estimated arrival updates the flight and is visible immediately on GET /flights. Rate-limited per traveler: too many sync requests return 429 with a Retry-After header. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric flight ID. Returns 403 if the authenticated traveler does not track this flight — including when no flight with that id exists, so the response does not reveal whether a flight id is real to someone who does not track it.

get.description: Returns all lounges at the specified airport, each annotated with whether the authenticated traveler is eligible to access it. Eligibility is computed from the traveler's loyalty memberships and tier benefits. Query parameter: airportIata — the IATA airport code (e.g. 'LHR', 'JFK'). An airport with no lounges is an empty list, not a 404 — this route never reports one. Returns 400 if airportIata is missing or is not a 3-letter IATA code.
Returns loyalty programs linked to the specified airline IATA code (e.g. 'BA'). Use this to populate the program picker when the user knows their airline.
Returns a paginated list of airline loyalty programs, including their full tier hierarchy. Use this to populate program/tier picker UIs. Supports ?page and ?pageSize (default 50, max 200).
Returns a paginated list of the authenticated traveler's loyalty memberships. Supports ?page and ?pageSize (default 50, max 200).

post.summary: Add a loyalty membership
post.description: Links a loyalty program membership to the authenticated traveler. Body fields: ProgramId (from GET /loyalty/programs), AccountNumber, TierId (optional, from the program's tier list), TierExpiryDate (optional, YYYY-MM-DD), PointsExpiryDate (optional, YYYY-MM-DD).

put.description: Replaces the account number, tier, and expiry dates for the specified membership. Route parameter: id — the membership ID returned when it was added. Only the authenticated traveler's own memberships can be updated. Returns 404 if no membership with that id exists, and 403 if it belongs to another traveler.

delete.description: Deletes a loyalty membership from the authenticated traveler's profile. Route parameter: id — the membership ID to remove. Idempotent: removing a membership that does not exist also returns 204, so there is no 404. Returns 403 if the membership belongs to another traveler.

post.summary: Register traveler
post.description: Creates a traveler profile linked to the authenticated Azure AD B2C identity. Idempotent — safe to call on every login; does nothing if the traveler already exists.

get.description: Returns the authenticated traveler's profile. Display name is owned by Azure AD B2C and is refreshed from the sign-in token on each login; it is read-only here.

post.summary: Register device token
post.description: Registers a push notification device token for the authenticated traveler. Currently supports iOS (APNs). The token is used to send flight status alerts when notifications are enabled for a tracked flight.

get.description: Returns all push notification device tokens registered for the authenticated traveler.

delete.description: Removes a previously registered push notification device token. Use this when a user logs out or when the OS invalidates the token. Route parameter: deviceTokenId — the ID of the device token to remove. Idempotent in the token: removing one that is already gone returns 204. The 404 means the traveler is not registered — call POST /travelers first.

Bearer.description: Enter 'Bearer' followed by a space and the JWT.
